Never a silent no-op.\\n# Protocol: issues and pull requests\\n\\nNormative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in\\n`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is\\n`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for\\nissues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*\\nhere and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no\\nshadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error\\nfails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).\\n\\n## 1. Records, names, tools\\n\\nIssues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,\\nno frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation\\n(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the\\nretired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the\\nrepository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a\\nlabel absent from GitHub is reported, never invented. Briefs (the design record\\nper issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.\\n\\nPrerequisites between issues are **GitHub issue dependencies**\\n(`GET`/`POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`), one edge per prerequisite.\\nThe edge is retained even when the prerequisite closes, so reopening it restores the block.\\nA prerequisite carried by a pull request is the packet issue that PR closes. The\\n\\\"Dependencies\\\" bullets in an issue body are commentary on those edges, never\\nthe record. A packet is **ready** when it is an open leaf of the tracker tree\\nand every issue blocking it is closed; `local/bin/ready_packets.py` computes\\nthat list, and the operator launches lanes from it rather than from a\\nhand-kept order or a dependency table in a comment (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-04).\\nEstablish or adopt each edge with\\n`local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`. The command first\\nreads the edge, makes at most one mutation, and re-reads after an ambiguous\\nfailure; it is therefore safe to repeat. Record closed prerequisites too.\\n\\nEvery GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python\\ncallers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,\\n`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,\\n`issue-create`, `add-blocked-by`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists\\nthem) owning CLI discovery, repository resolution, API version headers,\\nbounded retry of transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention.\\nNothing else shells out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`,\\n`ci.sh`, `review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub\\nnumbers; `track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.\\n\\nEvery repository-owned branch publication runs through `checked-push.sh` with\\none explicit `refs/heads/...:refs/heads/...` mapping.  The helper reads the\\nremote tip with a short `ls-remote`, resolves the local ref's registered\\nworktree, and refuses a checkout whose HEAD or working tree differs from the\\ncaptured commit.  It runs that checkout's `.githooks/pre-push` against the exact\\nref tuple before starting `receive-pack`, then pushes the captured commit under\\nan exact remote-tip lease.  The native hook performs a short defense-in-depth\\ncomparison when selected, while the helper's lease makes a moved remote ref fail\\nclosed even when that hook is stale or absent.  A caller's explicit\\n`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` remains the documented emergency bypass.  It skips\\nvalidation only: implicit tag following stays disabled, so publication remains\\nlimited to the explicit branch mapping.\\n\\nEvery merge of `github/main` or a stack parent into an issue branch runs the\\nmerge-loss guard before the merge commit is created. The guard compares the\\npending index with `HEAD`, `MERGE_HEAD`, and every best merge base. It refuses\\nan incoming path that disappeared without a branch-side deletion and an\\nincoming-only entry restored wholesale to the unchanged branch blob. Paths\\nrecorded by Git as conflicts remain resolution decisions. The\\n`reference-transaction` hook checks an automatic merge's commit object before\\nthe branch ref moves; `pre-commit` checks the pending index for a merge\\ncommitted later. Neither path permits `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS` to bypass this\\ncheck. A lane checking an existing merge uses the primary checkout's\\n`local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py --repo <worktree> --commit <merge>` so a stale\\nbranch copy cannot weaken the audit.\\n\\n* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`\\n  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.\\n* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch\\n  names inherit those characters and \\\"`]` breaks part of the PR automation\\n  stack\\\" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine\\n  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.\\n* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes\\n  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the\\n  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain\\n  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.\\n* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does\\n  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that\\n  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.\\n\\n## 2. Evidence contracts\\n\\nAll evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).\\n\\n**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one\\n`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,\\n`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,\\n`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.\\n`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`\\nafter it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads\\nthe *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined\\nstatus, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one\\nPR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by\\n`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.\\n\\n**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,\\ncarrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the\\nline `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.\\nUnchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\\\\s*[-*]\\\\s*\\\\[ \\\\]`; clean means\\n`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`\\ntoo — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review\\nevent carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`\\n(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.\\n\\n**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with\\n`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition\\nline per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.\\n\\n**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated\\nread finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating\\nit (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than\\nwebhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.\\n\\n## 3. The merge gate\\n\\n`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,\\nnever push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact\\n`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge\\ncommit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates\\nthat refuse by default:\\n\\n1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely\\n   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;\\n2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip\\n   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;\\n3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on\\n   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state\\n   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;\\n4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per\\n   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or\\n   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is\\n   `success` there;\\n5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;\\n6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);\\n   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix\\n   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;\\n7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not\\n   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.\\n\\n`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when\\nan exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.\\n\\nAfterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the\\nremote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local\\ndirt defers it with a warning).\\n\\n## 4. Untrusted text\\n\\nIssue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive\\nfrom GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,\\nwrites the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into\\nagent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and\\n`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced\\ncode with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for\\nbodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).\\n\\nEvery LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on\\n`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != \\\"false\\\"`; read prompts from committed main\\n(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame\\nsanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed\\nlabel through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally\\nkeeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.\\n\\n## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive\\n\\n`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local\\nlocation); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read\\nfrom the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s\\nown loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with\\nthe reason recorded in `results/telemetry/events.md`, unlike\\n`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE` (the pre-commit budget), the one owner-gated control\\nin the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and\\n`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).\\n\\n`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only\\nsnapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`\\n(and, since the push goes through `checked-push.sh`, commits that snapshot and\\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` to the primary checkout so the next publish\\nfinds a clean tree)\\n(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the\\nissue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The\\nretired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit\\nc8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.\\n\\n## 6. Owner inbox and mathematical-gap escalation\\n\\nPinned issue #26 is the owner inbox: it receives only decisions that require\\nthe human owner. A source statement found to be mathematically false does not\\ngo there first. Following the availability report on #26 and the September 6\\nowner decision, main chooses Astra max/xhigh for the mathematical-gap lane through\\n`MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra local/bin/dispatch.sh --role mathfix --effort max`.\\nHistorical owner-launched Fable measurements remain unchanged. Every request or\\ndispatch carries the exact source path, label and line range; the counterexample\\nor obstruction; the paper-gap note; the relevant blueprint dependency graph and\\nLean consumers; and the cumulative session count and elapsed working time.\\n\\nA correction is adopted only when it meets all four conditions below.\\n\\n1. **Correctness:** the known counterexample no longer applies, adversarial\\n   checks find no replacement counterexample, and a mathematical proof sketch\\n   derives the corrected conclusion from its explicit hypotheses using cited\\n   source results.\\n2. **Sufficiency:** every use in the paper and every dependent node in the\\n   blueprint graph remains justified; checking only the first Lean consumer is\\n   insufficient.\\n3. **Minimality:** the correction is the closest sufficient statement to the\\n   source, with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change\\n   to a mathematical definition or game.\\n4. **Lean convergence:** the corrected statement type-checks and all affected\\n   downstream consumers compile. Lean success alone does not establish the\\n   preceding three conditions.\\n\\nThe operator iterates mathematics and Lean for at most ten `mathfix` sessions\\nor about one and a half working days per gap, whichever comes first. The budget\\nis shared across the historical owner-launched Fable lane and the Astra lane; a\\nmodel or telemetry change does not reset it. If the correction requires\\nchanging a mathematical definition or game, the operator stops and escalates\\nimmediately. If the ordinary budget expires without a converged correction,\\n#26 receives the attempted statements, counterexamples, proof sketches, and\\nunresolved consumer failures. A still-running attempt is not grounds to reset\\nthe count.\\n\\nAn adopted correction follows the ordinary CI and independent-review gates. The\\noperator announces it in one line on progress log #27 and records it in the\\npaper-gap note, `results/telemetry/events.md`, and\\n`results/telemetry/design-decisions.md`. That announcement informs the owner; it\\nis not a request for a decision.\\n# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns\\n\\nCatalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks\\n(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to\\nprove the claimed mathematics. Complements\\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\\nbake in*.\\n\\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\\n\\n## Why this matters\\n\\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\\n\\n- Be marked `\\\\leanok` in the blueprint,\\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\\n\\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\\ncodebase.\\n\\n## Catalogue\\n\\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\\n\\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\\nPR [#491].\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\\\leanok` tag\\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\\n  conclusion.\\n- The proof body is one of:\\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\\n\\n### Concrete example\\n\\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\\n\\n```lean\\ntheorem mainInduction\\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\\n```\\n\\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\\n\\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\\nthe preferred shape for new work.\\n\\nA signature passes the smell test if:\\n\\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\\n\\n### Related issues and patterns\\n\\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\\n\\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \\\"mathematical\\ncontent\\\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\\nissues [#477], [#494].\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \\\"proof\\\" transports none of the\\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\\nanywhere in Lean.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\\n  directly.\\n\\n### Concrete example\\n\\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\\n\\n```lean\\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\\n\\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\\n    (α β : Point params) :\\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\\n\\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\\n  · intro α β\\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\\n  ...\\n```\\n\\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\\ndefinition equals itself.\\n\\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\\n\\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\\n   concrete objects.\\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\\n\\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \\\"precondition not met.\\\" Downstream\\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \\\"the output\\\" is\\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\\nprecondition failed.\\n\\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\\n\\\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\\\" The Lean should\\nmatch.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\\n\\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\\n\\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\\n\\n```lean\\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\\n  match g with\\n  | some p => p.poly\\n  | none   => 0\\n```\\n\\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\\n\\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\\nas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\\nare visible at call sites.\\n\\n### Acceptable uses of this pattern\\n\\nNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\\nthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\\nany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \\\"the output satisfies\\nP\\\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\\nsmuggling a precondition.\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\nPick one of:\\n\\n1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\\n   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\\n   be passed.\\n2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\\n   the case, so theorems about \\\"the output\\\" now quantify only over the\\n   `some` branch.\\n3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\\n   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\\n   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\\n\\n### Classical-logic dependencies\\n\\nA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\\nthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\\nconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\\nimplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\\ngate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR\\n#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.\\nThose classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely\\nnon-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't\\nbottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of\\nclassical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#307] — placeholder Lagrange coefficient (original fallback tracker)\\n- [#495] — the full pasting-interpolation catalogue\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials\\n\\n**Smell.** A theorem of the shape `∃ x, P x` is closed by picking\\n`x := default`, `x := 0`, `x := 1`, or `x := Classical.arbitrary`, where the\\npaper names a *specific, non-trivial* `x` and derives `P x` from real\\nstructure. The Lean claim is *mathematically* weaker because the Lean\\ntheorem guarantees less than the paper's (it proves some-trivial-thing, not\\nthe-specific-paper-thing). See [#449] for the full ledger.\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\nThe theorem name matches a paper lemma but the witness has been cheapened\\ninto a placeholder. Downstream theorems that inspect the witness get `0` or\\n`default`, which is almost always useless. Consumers that \\\"use\\\" the lemma\\nare really using the trivial `∃` and cannot proceed past the first attempt\\nto pin the witness down.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- `refine ⟨default, ?_⟩` / `exact ⟨default, ...⟩` / `refine ⟨0, ?_⟩` /\\n  `exact ⟨1, ...⟩` inside a proof of a paper-cited existential.\\n- `letI : Inhabited X := ⟨Classical.arbitrary X⟩` followed by a `let x :=\\n  default`.\\n- `Classical.arbitrary` / `Classical.choice` / `Nonempty.some` in proof\\n  bodies (as opposed to typeclass definitions).\\n- Identifier suffix `...Witness := default` on a bundled output.\\n\\n### Concrete example\\n\\nFrom the ledger in [#449]:\\n\\n- `lem:sdp` / `sdp` — primal witness is `T := default` (a zero\\n  submeasurement) and dual witness `Z := 1`. The paper requires a specific\\n  feasible pair; the Lean version proves only that some arbitrary pair exists,\\n  which always does.\\n- `lem:projective-low-rank-sum` / `projectiveLowRankSum` — auxiliary\\n  projective measurement `t := (default : ProjMeas Outcome ι)`. The paper\\n  constructs `(auxSpace, T_a)` from the eigenvector basis of each rounded\\n  `R_a`; the Lean version picks a zero-dimensional placeholder, which is\\n  disconnected from the paper's SVD derivation.\\n- ~~`lem:global-rewrite` / `globalRewrite` — decomposition witness is\\n  `default`~~ (historical; resolved by PRs #527 and #542). The live theorem now\\n  uses `canonicalGlobalVarianceDecomposition`, and\\n  `globalVarianceTraceWitness` consumes the centered residual family\\n  `u ↦ A^u - A_{\\\\mathrm{avg}}` rather than ignoring the witness.\\n\\n### Acceptable uses\\n\\nNon-computable instances required for typeclass plumbing, such as\\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)` inhabited by the zero polynomial, are fine when\\nthey are used only to *inhabit* a type, not to discharge a paper-cited\\nexistential.  Degenerate measurements should be constructed explicitly with a\\nspecified outcome rather than supplied by an ambient `Inhabited` instance.  The\\nsmell is specifically about `default` showing up in the proof of a *theorem\\nnamed after a paper result*.\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\n- Construct the paper's witness explicitly. If the ingredients are not yet\\n  formalized (e.g., Mathlib SVD, spectral decomposition), extract a bridge\\n  lemma that *constructs* the witness from the missing Mathlib facts, and\\n  track the Mathlib gap as a separate issue.\\n- Keep the existential statement, but strengthen the conclusion so that\\n  `x := default` no longer satisfies it (e.g., \\\"there exists `x` *with*\\n  rank `m`\\\", not merely \\\"there exists `x`\\\").\\n- If the witness cannot yet be constructed, keep the source-facing existential\\n  statement and expose the missing construction as a named proof obligation.\\n  Replacing `default` by an explicit bridge hypothesis is still an A1-grade\\n  placeholder, not a proof of the paper theorem.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#449] — master ledger; all three known cases are already listed\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib\\n\\n**Smell.** Lean code re-declares or re-proves something that already lives\\nin Mathlib, or builds a tower of custom lemmas that never bottom out in\\nMathlib / Lean core. The proof \\\"works\\\" only because the internal custom\\nstatements are compatible with each other — it is a closed ecosystem that\\ndoesn't ground in the reference library.\\n\\nThis is the \\\"scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\\" section of\\n[`project_conventions.md`](./project_conventions.md) in concrete examples. The two\\nflavours:\\n\\n1. **Re-proving Mathlib.** Writing `private lemma my_add_comm : a + b = b + a`\\n   when `add_comm` exists.\\n2. **Custom types that shadow Mathlib.** Defining `MyMeasurement` instead of\\n   using `MeasureTheory.Measure`, `MyMatrix` instead of `Matrix`,\\n   `MyHermitian` instead of `Matrix.IsHermitian`. The custom version may be\\n   definitionally equal to (or coercible from) the Mathlib version, but if\\n   it isn't, every consumer must reprove everything.\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\n1. The duplicated statements aren't audited by Mathlib's community, so they\\n   may be subtly wrong (wrong edge case, wrong universe, wrong typeclass).\\n2. When the real Mathlib proof is needed (for a key gap lemma), the custom\\n   tower must be rewritten to interoperate — often via a painful coercion\\n   layer that reintroduces every fact.\\n3. Hides real Mathlib gaps. If we decline to use Mathlib because \\\"our\\n   version is simpler,\\\" the gap never gets filed against Mathlib.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- `private lemma` in a file about well-established algebra/analysis\\n  (Cauchy–Schwarz, `sqrt`, `rpow`, `PosSemidef`, `Matrix.trace`, etc.).\\n- Custom structures named `MyX` / `LocalX` / `ProjectX` where `X` is a\\n  standard concept.\\n- Proof bodies that chain ten `private lemma`s where the natural Mathlib\\n  counterpart would be two `exact?` lookups.\\n- Files with no `import Mathlib.*` above the level of `Mathlib.Tactic.*`\\n  when the subject matter is clearly Mathlib-adjacent (linear algebra,\\n  analysis, measure theory).\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\nBefore writing a new lemma, spend one minute on:\\n\\n- `exact?` / `apply?` on the goal.\\n- `#find` / `Loogle` for the statement shape.\\n- `rg -n \\\"theorem.*X\\\" .lake/packages/mathlib/` for a keyword.\\n\\nIf Mathlib has it, use it. If it doesn't, consider whether the missing\\nlemma should be upstreamed (file an issue against Mathlib, or at least a\\nTODO pointing at the gap). The project already has this mandate — see the\\n\\\"Mathlib Integration\\\" section of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):\\n\\n> Scout Mathlib first (`exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source)\\n\\nA5 is what happens when that step is skipped.\\n\\n### Audit cross-reference\\n\\n`audits/` contains chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency scouting\\nreports. If a section of the code review says \\\"this could use Mathlib\\nlemma X\\\", it belongs in a specific `audits/*.md` file for that chapter.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles\\n\\n**Smell.** A theorem takes a hypothesis of type `SomeStatement` (or\\n`SomeWitness`, `SomeOutput`, etc.) that is defined elsewhere and intended\\nto represent an external mathematical result, but there is no theorem\\nconstructing it from the hypotheses under which the paper uses it. The Lean\\nstatement is then:\\n\\\"assuming the external result, the Lean conclusion holds.\\\" That is\\nsometimes legitimate (e.g., a cite to a book whose formalization we don't\\nplan to do), and sometimes a cover for locally-unwanted work.\\n\\nThis overlaps with A1 but is subtler: the hypothesis isn't the\\n*current theorem's* conclusion, it's an *independently-named* claim that\\nhappens to unblock the current proof.\\n\\n### Acceptable external smuggles\\n\\n- **Genuine external citations.** `PolishchukSpielmanClassicalSoundnessStatement`\\n  cites the Polishchuk–Spielman theorem; we don't plan to formalize it.\\n- **Mathlib gaps we can't fill.** `hMatrixChernoff` in `chernoffBernoulliMatrix`\\n  is a Mathlib matrix-Chernoff-type statement; we flagged the gap upstream.\\n- **Tracked internal obligations.** A `*Statement` that has an open sub-issue\\n  and a named construction theorem target is trackable proof debt. It is still\\n  not an acceptable extra hypothesis on a source-labelled paper theorem.\\n\\n### Unacceptable external smuggles\\n\\n- A `*Statement` with no open tracking issue, no docstring explaining the\\n  mathematical gap, and no consumer-side comment flagging the smuggle.\\n- A `*Statement` whose body is the theorem's conclusion, wearing a different\\n  name (A1 in disguise).\\n- A `*Statement` used to close a lemma whose paper version does not require\\n  any such external assumption (silent strengthening of the Lean theorem\\n  relative to the paper's).\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\nGrep for these suffixes: `*Statement`, `*Witness`, `*Claim`,\\n`*Conclusion`, `*Output`, `*Input`, `*Hypothesis`, `*Requirement`,\\n`*Assumption`, `*Package` (that isn't a `*BridgePackage`). For each, ask:\\n\\n- Is there a theorem anywhere that **constructs** a value of this type from the\\n  paper hypotheses?\\n- If not, is the absence explained in a docstring / tracking issue /\\n  `audits/` entry?\\n- Does the paper depend on an external theorem of this shape?\\n\\nIf any answer is \\\"no\\\", the structure is an unacceptable smuggle.\\n\\n### Current status (audited 2026-05-08)\\n\\nThe May 2026 re-audit\\n([`audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md`](../blob/main/audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md))\\nclassified 39 `*Statement` structures (102 declarations total across the\\nextended suffix sweep of `*Witness`/`*Conclusion`/`*Input`/etc.).\\n\\nThe live ledger is [#1379], replacing the now-closed [#449] (2026-05-01) and\\n[#451] (2026-04-30). Headline counts from the re-audit: 33 grounded, 2 tracked\\nsmuggle, 2 external citation, 1 paper-faithful packaging, 1 dead. Without a live\\nledger, **5 `*Statement` structures landed between 2026-04-18 and 2026-05-08\\nwithout a tracker entry** — the gap this policy fixes.\\n\\nThe Section 5 spectral-truncation chain is now an example of the preferred\\nmigration: the old `SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation has been removed, and\\nlater arguments call direct constructors for `SpectralTruncationStatement`\\ninstead of carrying an `Input` wrapper.\\n\\nIf you add a new `*Statement`-style structure to this codebase, include a\\ndef-site docstring with its paper origin (per the \\\"earn your place\\\" policy in\\n[#1379]). If no construction theorem exists yet, file a sub-issue in [#1379]\\nand ship the source-faithful construction theorem with an explicit unfinished\\nproof obligation. Do not add the structure as a new source-theorem hypothesis\\nmerely to keep downstream declarations compiling.\\n\\n### Merge gate — new `*Statement` / `*Witness` / `*Input` structures\\n\\nTo prevent dead scaffolds from landing unnoticed (the 5-structure gap of\\n2026-04-18–2026-05-08), every PR that introduces a new `structure XStatement`,\\n`structure XWitness`, `structure XInput`, `abbrev XStatement`, or\\n`abbrev XInput` must satisfy **at least one** of these before merge:\\n\\n1. **Has a construction theorem.** A theorem that constructs a value of this\\n   type from the appropriate paper hypotheses appears in the same PR or an\\n   already-merged ancestor. If the proof is not finished, the theorem must carry\\n   the explicit tracked proof obligation rather than moving the assertion into a\\n   paper-facing theorem's hypotheses.\\n2. **Has a consumer.** A theorem that takes a value of this type as a\\n   hypothesis appears in the same PR or an already-merged ancestor.\\n3. **Has a ledger entry.** A classification comment (G / E / T / P / D, per\\n   the verdict key in [#1379]) is posted on [#1379] as an issue comment, and\\n   the structure's def-site docstring links to that comment.\\n\\nStructures that satisfy none of the above are dead on arrival and must not\\nmerge.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#1379] — live `*Statement` ledger (replaces closed [#449] / [#451])\\n- [#449] — historical paper-wide gap tracker (closed 2026-05-01)\\n- [#451] — historical bridge-hypothesis tracker (closed 2026-04-30)\\n- [#278] — the original \\\"derive `PermInvState` internally\\\" discussion\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Reviewer checklist\\n\\nUse this alongside the blocker\\nlist in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)\\nchecklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper\\nresult, ask:\\n\\n- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the\\n      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.\\n- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If\\n      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match\\n      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.\\n- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if\\n      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature\\n      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.\\n- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an\\n      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness\\n      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.\\n- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a\\n      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it\\n      (A5).\\n- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /\\n      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its\\n      grounding plan (A6)?\\n- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's\\n      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences\\n      as ⚠️S in [#1379].\\n\\nA lemma that passes all of these is a proof. A lemma that fails one is\\nscaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with\\n`\\\\leanok` until the gap is closed).\\n\\n## CI prevention\\n\\nMechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:\\n\\n- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use\\n  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current\\n  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation. It parses\\n  theorem/lemma headers and warns when an explicit existential hypothesis shares\\n  the conclusion's salient structure, while printing witness-adapter helpers\\n  separately. When [#438] lands (`\\\\leanok` ↔ `sorryAx` drift), extend the same\\n  idea to all `\\\\leanok`-tagged declarations: parse the hypothesis list; if any\\n  hypothesis's type (modulo `∃`/`∀`/`∧`) contains a prefix of the conclusion\\n  structure, warn.\\n- **A2 (definitional sleight).** Grep for `theorem <Name>.* := rfl` where\\n  `<Name>` has a blueprint `\\\\lean{}` cross-reference. The only allowed cases\\n  are ones annotated with `@[paper_bookkeeping]` (proposed attribute) or in\\n  an allow-list.\\n- **A3 (zero-fallback).** Grep for identifier suffixes `fallback`, `or0`,\\n  `orDefault`, `placeholder`, `sentinel` in `Defs/*` files. Each should have\\n  a docstring citing the downstream eligibility precondition.\\n- **A4 (default witnesses).** Grep `:= default`, `refine ⟨default`, `exact\\n  ⟨default`, `Classical.arbitrary` inside proof bodies (not typeclass\\n  definitions). Cross-reference to [#1379]'s witness ledger.\\n- **A5 (Mathlib bypass).** No reliable CI check, but `audits/` reports\\n  catch it during per-chapter audits.\\n- **A6 (external smuggles).** Every new `structure *Statement` without a\\n  producing theorem should be required to carry a `/-- Grounded by: #NNN\\n  -/` docstring, enforced by a lint rule over `blueprint/`.\\n\\nThe scripts in `scripts/` (notably `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py` and\\n`scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`) are the natural home for extensions that\\nadd these checks.\\n\\n## See also\\n\\n- the lean-conventions https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/1379\\n# Mathematical Language Guidelines\\n\\nMIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing\\nthe formalization with the paper and blueprint.\\n\\nThis is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,\\nnaming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,\\n`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\n\\n## Scope\\n\\nThese guidelines apply to:\\n\\n- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;\\n- module docstrings;\\n- declaration docstrings;\\n- documentation-visible section comments;\\n- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.\\n- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;\\n- issue titles and issue bodies;\\n- PR titles and PR descriptions.\\n\\n## Source of Truth\\n\\nUse terminology from the following sources, in this order:\\n\\n1. `references/ldt-paper/`\\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`\\n3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files\\n\\nWhen the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for\\nexample, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to\\nprojectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.\\n\\n## Reference Notation And Terminology\\n\\nThe notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for\\nreader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean\\ndocstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source\\nwithout first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.\\n\\nWhen Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a\\nlocation which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the\\nfirst applicable location in the following order:\\n\\n1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation\\n   differs from the paper;\\n2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a\\n   family of declarations in that file;\\n3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the\\n   blueprint;\\n4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a\\n   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.\\n\\nThe explanation should say:\\n\\n- the notation or term used in the paper;\\n- the Lean object or name which represents it;\\n- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;\\n- the scope in which the replacement should be used.\\n\\nA PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place\\nwhere future readers can learn it.\\n\\nFormalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose\\nshould name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,\\nrather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.\\n\\n## Naming Norm\\n\\nNames and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or\\nconclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was\\nassembled.\\n\\nAvoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,\\n`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source\\nuses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes\\nsuch as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a\\nclearer phrase.\\n\\nThis is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.\\nModule names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,\\nblueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the\\nmathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line\\nnumber, or implementation history.\\n\\n### Concrete examples\\n\\nThe table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the\\ncodebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;\\nothers are proposed names for future refactors.  The \\\"avoid\\\" column lists\\nprocess-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was\\nassembled; the \\\"prefer\\\" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the\\npaper or blueprint would recognize.\\n\\n| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |\\n|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not \\\"the line-130 identity\\\"          |\\n| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |\\n| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |\\n| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |\\n| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |\\n| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |\\n| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |\\n| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an \\\"unwrapped\\\" version |\\n| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |\\n| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |\\n\\nAn avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that\\nphrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls \\\"Step 2\\\").\\nIn that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.\\n\\nFile-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be\\nnamed by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations\\nexposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.\\n\\n### Shared helpers\\n\\nWhen the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or\\nmore chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single\\nshared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and\\nensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all\\ncall sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.\\n\\nProcedure:\\n\\n1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the\\n   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,\\n   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),\\n   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or\\n   explicit argument.\\n2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by\\n   both call sites.  Typical candidates:\\n   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,\\n   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,\\n   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.\\n3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes\\n   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.\\n4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace\\n   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it\\n   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers\\n   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility\\n   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that\\n   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.\\n5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or\\n   blueprint location it supports.\\n\\n### Legacy identifier treatment\\n\\nIf a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and\\ndescribe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public\\nidentifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration\\nin the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.\\n\\nDo not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second\\npublic name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the\\nshared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or\\nblueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.\\n\\n## Review Checklist\\n\\nReviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and\\ndocumentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.\\n\\n- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,\\n      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,\\n      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the\\n      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,\\n      implementation-phase labels)?\\n- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does\\n      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the\\n      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,\\n      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the\\n      source does not use them that way?\\n- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from\\n      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,\\n      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in\\n      that order of preference?\\n- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced\\n      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or\\n      construction they support?\\n- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists\\n      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf? Neither runtime tree is committed.\\n\\n```\\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\\n└── hot-main/\\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\\n    │   └── info\\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\\n    ├── snapshots/\\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\\n```\\n\\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\\ncalls and no name parsing.\\n\\n### `STAMP` schema\\n\\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\\n\\n```\\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\\nstatus=complete|partial\\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\\nwarmer_version=1\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\\n\\n```\\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\\n                          [--targets \\\"<lake targets>\\\"] [--lock-timeout S]\\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\\n```\\n\\n### 5.1 Writer lease\\n\\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\\n\\nStaleness is decided in this order:\\n\\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\\n\\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\\nprevent.\\n\\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\\n\\n### 5.2 Build\\n\\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\\n   finish, then warm again.\\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\\n   **No `lake update`.**\\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\\n   prompts may later read.\\n\\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\\n\\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\\n\\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\\n\\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\\n\\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\\n\\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\\n\\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\\nso loudly.\\n\\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\\\"main did not build cleanly\\\"* —\\nnot *\\\"nothing was published.\\\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\\nreason to retry.\\n\\n### 5.5 Retention\\n\\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\\n\\n```\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\\n```\\n\\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\\n\\nDecision procedure:\\n\\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\\n\\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\\n\\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\\n\\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\\n  clone;\\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\\n\\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\\n\\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\\n\\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\\n\\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\\n\\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\\nlocking there.\\n\\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\\n\\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\\nwhat a stale lock is.\\n\\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\\n\\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\\n\\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \\\"no pid, therefore\\n  stale\\\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\\n  field is read as \\\"this host\\\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\\n\\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\\n\\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\\n   error.\\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\\n   if the pin is not already installed.\\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\\n   exists to prevent.\\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\\\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\\\"*\\n\\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\\nif anything is missing.\\n\\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\\n\\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\\n\\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\\n\\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\\n\\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\\n\\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\\nfetching.\\n\\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\\nsource.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 9. Telemetry\\n\\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\\n\\n```jsonc\\n{\\\"ts\\\": \\\"<ISO 8601 with offset>\\\",\\n \\\"kind\\\": \\\"warm\\\" | \\\"rebuild\\\" | \\\"cache-get\\\",\\n \\\"trigger\\\": \\\"<who asked for this>\\\",\\n \\\"outcome\\\": \\\"success\\\" | \\\"failed\\\",\\n \\\"seconds\\\": <int>,\\n \\\"sha\\\": \\\"<commit, when known>\\\",\\n \\\"note\\\": \\\"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\\\"}\\n```\\n\\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\\n\\nThree properties are load-bearing:\\n\\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 10. Operating procedures\\n\\n```bash\\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\\n\\n# What is published right now?\\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\\n\\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\\n\\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\\n\\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\\n\\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\\n```\\n\\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\\n\\n| condition | behaviour |\\n|---|---|\\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 12.
